testProcedure: TP-101: User Access & Authentication Review
title: Semi-Annual User Access review exclusion of dormant users with access
header: Semi-Annual User Access review exclusion of dormant users with access
issue:
The Semi-Annual User Access review performed in November 2025 does not include dormant users with active access within CoStar, resulting in an incomplete user listing.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-07 Section No. [10] - Semi-Annual User Access Certification — Dormant accounts with active access must be identified and recertified
2. S-07 Section No. [9] - Privileged User Access Recertification Review — Comprehensive user listing required for periodic recertification
originalIssue:
The Semi-Annual User Access review performed in November 2025 does not include dormant users with active access within CoStar, resulting in an incomplete user listing.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-07 Section No. [10] - Semi-Annual User Access Certification — Dormant accounts with active access must be identified and recertified
2. S-07 Section No. [9] - Privileged User Access Recertification Review — Comprehensive user listing required for periodic recertification
rootCause: The user access review process was not designed to include dormant users with active access within CoStar.
impact: Dormant users with active access could exploit or misuse the system, potentially leading to unauthorized transactions, data manipulation, or exposure of sensitive information.
recommendation:
1. Update the Semi-Annual User Access review process to identify and address dormant users with active access within CoStar.

2. Define criteria to identify dormant users based on a specified period of inactivity.

3. Revoke access for dormant users unless management provides and documents a valid business justification.

4. Management should implement a monitoring mechanism to periodically review and validate the effectiveness of the updated user access review process.

5. Train relevant personnel on the updated process to promote proper execution and accountability.
managementResponse: Management agrees with the finding. Global Access Management will update the CoStar semi-annual recertification charter to mandate automated identification and deprovisioning of accounts dormant beyond 90 days, with supervisory sign-off workflows.
summaryFinding: Semi-annual access recertification omitted dormant accounts across the CoStar ERP application, presenting an unauthorized privileged access risk across 140 active credentials.
auditorResponse: Internal Audit verified that 140 dormant user accounts remained enabled in CoStar for over 180 consecutive days without formal supervisory exception approval.
mitigatingControl: Compensating database monitoring query is executed monthly by IT Security, though automated deprovisioning was absent.
exceptionRemedComments: Management has initiated a system enhancement request (CR-8821) to automate account suspension after 90 days of inactivity.

testProcedure: TP-103: Automated Telemetry & Calibration Logging Review
title: Catheter Line 3 optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2%
header: Catheter Line 3 optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2%
issue:
Optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2% tolerance threshold during continuous electrophysiology catheter assembly runs across 72 consecutive operating hours.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-12 Section No. [3.4] - Automated System Telemetry Logging & Monitoring — Sensor calibration drift exceeds acceptable operating tolerance limits
2. S-12 Section No. [8.1] - Hardware Integrity & Recalibration Protocols — Mandatory gain verification cycles omitted during multi-batch production
originalIssue:
Optic sensor telemetry gain calibration drift exceeding 4.2% tolerance threshold during continuous electrophysiology catheter assembly runs across 72 consecutive operating hours.

Violation Reference
Non-Compliant with some of the sections of IAPP:
1. S-12 Section No. [3.4] - Automated System Telemetry Logging & Monitoring — Sensor calibration drift exceeds acceptable operating tolerance limits
2. S-12 Section No. [8.1] - Hardware Integrity & Recalibration Protocols — Mandatory gain verification cycles omitted during multi-batch production
rootCause: Thermal dissipation latency in cleanroom HVAC Unit 4 created secondary optic gain drift during peak batch cycles, causing uncompensated sensor offsets.
impact: Potential delay in batch release and risk of $120,000 material scrap variance if unmitigated. Non-compliance with FDA GxP 21 CFR Part 11 records.
recommendation:
1. Upgrade sensor firmware to v4.2 enabling auto thermal offset compensation.
2. Establish real-time telemetry threshold alerts on IT Monitoring Console.
3. Enforce dual MFA authorization for manual sensor override calibrations.
managementResponse: Engineering will deploy telemetry calibration firmware v4.2 across all Catheter lines by end of Q3.
summaryFinding: Automated optical sensor telemetry logs on Catheter Assembly Line 3 demonstrated thermal gain drift exceeding the 1.5% SLA tolerance across 72 hours of production.
auditorResponse: Telemetry data logs confirmed 14 distinct excursions where gain offsets triggered manual supervisor override without root-cause ticket generation.
mitigatingControl: Post-assembly optical inspection station filters finished catheter batches prior to sterilization, preventing defective batch release.
exceptionRemedComments: Cleanroom HVAC Unit 4 thermal balance valve replacement scheduled; firmware patch v4.2 in validation testing.
impactedMrc: MRC-01: Global Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations
